Class DevManifest

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.dev.manifest.DevManifest
public final class DevManifest extends Object
What a build tool tells the development launcher about the project: the classpaths, the roots, how to compile, what to retain. Written as a java.util.Properties file, every key under micronaut.dev., so that a build can write it from its model without running anything and any key can be overridden with a system property of the same name.

Paths are resolved against the manifest's own directory unless absolute. A list is separated by commas or the platform's path separator; a value starting with @ names an argument file holding one entry per line, which keeps long classpaths off the command line.

micronaut.dev.main-class=example.Application
micronaut.dev.project-dir=.
micronaut.dev.strategy=auto
micronaut.dev.patch-in-place=true
micronaut.dev.runtime-classpath=@runtime.argfile
micronaut.dev.reloadable=build/classes/java/main,build/resources/main
micronaut.dev.compile-classpath=@compile.argfile
micronaut.dev.processor-path=@processors.argfile
micronaut.dev.sources.java=src/main/java
micronaut.dev.resources.config=src/main/resources
micronaut.dev.resources.views=src/main/resources/views
micronaut.dev.compile.mode=embedded
micronaut.dev.compile.incremental=true
micronaut.dev.compile.java.output=build/classes/java/main
micronaut.dev.compile.java.generated-sources=build/generated/sources/annotationProcessor/java/main
micronaut.dev.compile.java.options=-parameters,--release,21,-Amicronaut.processing.group=example
micronaut.dev.build-tool=gradle
micronaut.dev.build-tool.trigger=build/micronaut-dev/reload
micronaut.dev.retain=javax.sql.DataSource
micronaut.dev.max-generations=10
micronaut.dev.requests.hold-timeout=30s
micronaut.dev.requests.drain-timeout=10s
micronaut.dev.requests.retain-sockets=true

    • NATIVE_MAX_GENERATIONS

      public static final int NATIVE_MAX_GENERATIONS
      The generation budget in a native image, where the classes of a retired generation are never unloaded: GraalVM's runtime class loading keeps every class it defines, in a metaspace whose size is fixed when the image is built, and the interpreter's data for them on the heap, for the life of the process. Measured on a Pyronaut application whose generations each hold a GraalPy context, adding a route per generation: once a retired generation is released, what stays is its classes and their data, about 1.3 MB of heap a generation, and the resident memory of 61 generations stayed under 1 GB, with the metaspace not exhausted. Fifty bounds that growth with room to spare.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • patchInPlace

      public boolean patchInPlace()
      Whether a change of resources alone is offered to the running application's InPlaceResourceReloaders before a restart, so that, for example, a Python module whose generated classes did not change is patched into the running interpreters instead of starting a new generation. On by default, under every strategy: patching defines no class, so it needs no agent and is not what restart opts out of. micronaut.dev.patch-in-place=false turns it off.
      Returns:
      Whether resources may be patched in place

    • maxGenerations

      public int maxGenerations()
      The generation budget, micronaut.dev.max-generations: how many generations the runtime creates in one process. When a reload would create one more, the runtime closes and the launcher exits with MicronautDevMain.RELAUNCH, for whoever started it to start it again. Unlimited, zero, on the JVM, which unloads a retired generation once nothing refers to it; NATIVE_MAX_GENERATIONS in a native image, which never does. unlimited or 0 lifts it. Test mode runs its tests on a generation of their own from the second on, and checks the budget after a run, so that a run is never lost to the relaunch: watching, it takes at least three, or two without a first run, and run once it takes any.
      Returns:
      The budget, zero when unlimited

    • requestHoldTimeout

      public Duration requestHoldTimeout()
      How long a request that arrives while a batch is processed is held, "micronaut.dev.requests.hold-timeout": it is served once the batch is done, by the generation that runs then, or answered with a 503 and a Retry-After when the batch takes longer. 30 seconds by default.

    • requestDrainTimeout

      public Duration requestDrainTimeout()
      How long a restart waits for the requests in flight on the stopping generation, "micronaut.dev.requests.drain-timeout": they finish on the generation they started on. 10 seconds by default: a connection that never finishes, such as a websocket or an event stream, holds each restart this long.
      Returns:
      The timeout
